decisions.reason: As a close-to-core upholstery fabric with its own product page, A likely met at least modest aspirations and a medium-sized firm in a growing market has enough slack to keep it while demand develops.

B fits the firm's established decorative textile range, but its lower website prominence suggests slightly weaker early traction, so it is more vulnerable than the most highlighted launches yet still likely to be retained.
C combines a core curtain application with flame-retardant functionality and dedicated website presentation, which makes it likely to satisfy aspirations in both residential and contract segments.

D builds on the existing offer and benefits from the firm's broad assortment strategy, but as a wool-blend decorative fabric with only limited website emphasis it faces somewhat higher risk if early results are merely average.

E is adjacent to the firm's established portfolio and the firm has organizational slack to continue testing it, though its niche material-construction combination and limited web emphasis make it one of the more droppable products if performance disappoints.
